concepts.quote: First min = data[0], then i = 1, compare data[1] with min, if it is smaller min changes, then i = 2, and so on to the end; then it prints min
concepts.why: The answer walks through the running-minimum steps in order: start at data[0], compare each element and update when smaller, then print after the loop. It does not explain why the plan works.
The answer uses assignment correctly to set and update min, but it does not explain or trace how assignment evaluates and stores the value.
The answer never mentions Integer.MIN_VALUE or MAX_VALUE. It starts from data[0] instead.
